h: Making a Day of the Spen Valley
p: Ponderosa is the kind of zoo where you don't need to rush, and that's half the fun. Take your time around the lake, spend a while in the lemur walkthrough, and stop for a brew when you need to. It's well suited to younger children, who can manage the whole site comfortably, and the community feel makes it welcoming for everyone. Dress for the weather, bring wellies after a wet spell, and keep an eye on the talks and feeds if you want to catch the animals at their busiest.

Heckmondwike is a former mill town in the Spen Valley, and its proximity to the M62 makes it easy to reach from across West Yorkshire and beyond. If you've got time to spare after your visit, there are some lovely local spots to explore.

Oakwell Hall, in Birstall, is a historic Elizabethan manor house set in a country park, and fans of Charlotte Brontë might know it as the inspiration for Fieldhead in her novel Shirley. The surrounding park has woodland walks, a café and plenty of space to explore. In Batley, the Bagshaw Museum is a quirky local museum in a grand Victorian house, set in Wilton Park, with everything from local history to collections from around the world. The Spen Valley Greenway, a traffic-free walking and cycling route along an old railway line, is a handy place for a stroll or a bike ride with the kids. Leeds, Huddersfield and Bradford are all within easy reach for a bigger day out too.
